title: How much life insurance do you need?
summary: Rules of thumb: 10–12x income, plus debts, minus assets; a needs analysis beats any rule.

key_points: Rules of thumb: 10–12x income, plus debts, minus assets
a needs analysis beats any rule

sections.heading: Key points
sections.body: How much life insurance do you need?. Rules of thumb: 10–12x income, plus debts, minus assets; a needs analysis beats any rule.

sections.heading: In depth
sections.body: Start with the DIME method: Debts, Income replacement (years × income), Mortgage, Education. Subtract liquid assets. Then sanity-check affordability — the best policy is one you keep paying. Revisit after marriages, births, and mortgages. Educational content only — not financial advice. Consult a licensed insurance professional for your situation.

title: Whole life insurance
summary: Permanent coverage with level premiums, a cash value that grows, and dividends possible from mutual insurers.

key_points: Permanent coverage with level premiums, a cash value that grows, and dividends possible from mutual insurers

sections.heading: Key points
sections.body: Whole life insurance. Permanent coverage with level premiums, a cash value that grows, and dividends possible from mutual insurers.

sections.heading: In depth
sections.body: Whole life covers you for life as long as premiums are paid. Part of each premium funds the death benefit; part builds cash value that grows tax-deferred and can be borrowed against. Premiums are much higher than term for the same death benefit. Educational content only — not financial advice. Consult a licensed insurance professional for your situation.
